page: Amazon Web Services r7gd.medium is a memory-optimized virtual instance powered by a dedicated 64-bit ARM Neoverse-V1 core operating at 2.6 GHz under the AWS Nitro hypervisor. The instance pairs 1 dedicated physical core (1 vCPU) with 8.0 GB of RAM, offering a high 8:1 memory-to-core allocation. Cache provisions include 64 KB L1 data cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache. Local high-speed storage is integrated directly via a bundled 59 GB NVMe SSD instance store volume. Network bandwidth is provisioned at a 1 Gbps baseline, and there are no dedicated GPU accelerators.

Synthetic benchmark evaluations show stable single-threaded throughput balanced by structural multi-core throughput bounds. In single-core testing, the ARMv8 core records 1516.59 on stress-ng and 1440.0 on Geekbench, placing it in the mid-range performance tier. Data compression benchmarks reflect this capability, with single-threaded gzip achieving 23.82 GB/s and bzip3 decompression delivering 9.34 GB/s. Memory subsystem tests show cached read speeds up to 97.21 GB/s, while uncached 256 MB buffer transfers deliver 30.72 GB/s read and 10.9 GB/s write. Aggregate multi-core and multi-threaded metrics remain strictly limited due to the single-core topology.

From a resource-efficiency standpoint, the r7gd.medium serves applications that require elevated memory density and low-latency disk scratch space without requiring extensive thread concurrency. The direct integration of high-speed local NVMe storage reduces external block storage overhead for temporary files and local cache layers. The instance profile is aligned with lightweight Redis deployments, caching layers, small in-memory database replicas, and low-concurrency ETL pipeline processing.
